summary: Follow-up on an intermittent token leakage where stale KV entries caused cross-tenant responses under heavy batching. Agreed immediate data-dump + replay, short-term fallback config to disable cross-tenant KV reuse, and a deeper on-prem benchmark to validate isolation and latency impact.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28 UTC 15:00
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Cho (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ben Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (Redwood SRE advisor); Sophie Kim (BlueHarbor VP Eng), Raj Patel (BlueHarbor SRE), Maria Lopez (BlueHarbor ML Lead), Ethan Wu (BlueHarbor Platform)

Summary: Follow-up on the incident reported last week where some requests returned tokens associated with different tenants under bursty batching; we walked through hypotheses, requested artifacts, and agreed on a short-term mitigation + longer-term verification plan.

[00:00] Daniel (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this tight — the goal is to confirm what we need to reproduce the ghost token behavior and hand off to ops. Sophie, you had shared a brief timeline earlier, thanks for that.
[00:20] Sophie (BlueHarbor): yeah thanks, we had a few user sessions where the responses included product IDs from other tenants, it's low volume but high severity for us so we want it solved.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): quick prelim, we suspect a KV cache eviction / key collision under heavy continuous batching — essentially stale KV windows being re-used. But need logs and a small sample trace to be sure.
[00:52] Raj (BlueHarbor SRE): can you clarify — KV cache as in the Redwood runtime's kv cache or our redis? we run a fronting redis for shared session state.
[01:05] Priya: good call — in this case we mean Redwood's KV cache (the per-worker attention cache) not the customer's redis. but that distinction matters: if your fronting layer also multiplexes session IDs it could be compounding.
[01:25] Maria (ML Lead): to be explicit, we observed cross-tenant product ids in the generated completions, not raw key-value pairs from redis. the token strings map back to another account's dataset.
[01:41] Daniel: thanks, that helps. ok, we propose three parallel things: 1) Redwood to produce a trimmed KV dump from the timeframe, 2) BlueHarbor to run replay on a staging cluster and capture the request IDs, 3) short term config change to avoid cross-tenant reuse while we root cause. low risk?
[02:05] Sophie: yes that sounds right. Raj, will your team be able to run the replay?
[02:10] Raj: yes we can but need the exact replay script and the request ids. what format will the KV dump be?
[02:18] Priya: we'll provide a gzipped JSONL with timestamped entries with only the keys and sequence positions — we'll strip payloads for privacy. also include per-request routing metadata.
[02:31] Ethan (Platform): also, do you have an immediate fallback we can flip? we can't risk more cross-tenant hits.
[02:39] Maya (Redwood SRE advisor): short term we recommend per-tenant prefixing for KV keys plus a TTL tightening from default 24h to 1h for the hot window. that'll stop reuse even if eviction misaligns. it's a config toggle — minimal performance hit but reduces effective cache hit rate.
[02:58] Sophie: okay seems reasonable. what's the expected latency hit?
[03:05] Priya: rough estimate: 5–10% p50 token latency increase under peak heavy small-request workloads; p95 maybe 12% in synthetic bench, depends on your workload shape. that's why we want the microbenchmark.
[03:22] Maria: can you put that in a doc? CI bench numbers are helpful.
[03:27] Daniel: yes we'll share the microbench runbook and the prior numbers.
[03:32] 
[05:00] Raj: one clarification: the incident occurred during a sustained batch spike after our nightly job, so batch sizes went to ~512 for a short window. do you have any known issues at those batch sizes?
[05:12] Priya: our runtime supports continuous batching but we saw an internal bug in a prior release where under certain long tail patterns the KV index pointer could be off by one after ring wrap. we patched that in 1.8.3 but need to confirm your fleet was on 1.8.2 at the time.
[05:30] Ethan: we are on 1.8.2 in prod, will schedule upgrade but want to validate first.
[05:36] Maya: for immediate triage you'll want both logs: the worker local stdout around the window and the orchestration trace (route id -> worker id). the latter will show if a single worker served mixed tenant requests during the sticky period.
[05:52] Priya: exactly. and please capture stack traces if any OOM/retry happened. sometimes retries cause unexpected token cache reuse.
[06:05] Sophie: we didn't see OOMs, but there were a few 503s during the spike.
[06:12] Daniel: 503s can cause in-flight entries to be dropped in a way that later requests reuse a now-stale slot; it's consistent with our hypothesis.
[06:24] 
[08:00] Maria: high level question — if this is KV index drift, how likely is cross-tenant data exfil versus just correlated token mix? customers need confidence.
[08:12] Priya: current hypothesis is mis-attributed KV entries, not deliberate exfiltration. impact is limited to generated tokens that incidentally match other tenant data; still severe from privacy perspective. we'll need a deterministic replay to be sure.
[08:30] Raj: what about data residency and audit trail — can we get the audit logs for model inference calls?
[08:35] Ben (CSM): yes we can provide per-request audit logs exported from the console; I'll attach the export once we confirm which time range you want.
[08:46] Sophie: target window is 2026-02-21 02:00–02:30 UTC (the spike).
[08:53] Ben: noted.
[09:00] 
[12:00] Priya: on the replay — we'll provide a small harness (python) that replays request headers + prompt to a staging endpoint with deterministic RNG so tokens align. that will help us confirm whether it's reproducible with the same sequence.
[12:15] Maria: good. we will run on an iso'd staging cluster with same config as prod and send back result diffs.
[12:25] Daniel: also recommend enabling strict per-tenant namespace for the KV cache in your staging run to observe difference.
[12:32] Ethan: is namespace isolation available as a toggle or does it require code change?
[12:36] Maya: it's a runtime flag in 1.8.3, a config toggle. 1.8.2 lacks the full safety check.
[12:45] Raj: ok upgrading to 1.8.3 in staging first then replay — that gives us a comparison.
[13:00] 
[15:00] Sophie: security asks — we'll need SOC2 snapshot and your KMS/HSM details because we'll be doing a deeper audit if there's any cross-tenant leakage.
[15:12] Daniel: understood — I'll send the checklist and current SOC2 attestation, and a redacted HSM/KMS integration note.
[15:22] Ben: I'll include the audit logs export and a short note on access controls.
[15:30] 
[18:00] Maria: long-term, what changes are you planning at the runtime level to prevent index drift?
[18:10] Priya: dev team is adding stronger bounds checking for index wrap, additional unit tests for high-batch patterns, and a background scrubbing job that verifies prefix ownership for hot slots. that will roll into 1.9.0.
[18:25] Sophie: timeline? we need an ETA for the permanent fix.
[18:30] Priya: preliminary ETA is end of Q2 2026, but we'll prioritize a hotfix if replay shows it's a code regression.
[18:40] 
[22:00] Raj: operationally, if we flip per-tenant prefix + TTL tightening now, what's rollback?
[22:08] Maya: it's config only, rollback is immediate. we'll monitor cache hit rate. Prior to flipping, we'll snapshot baseline p50/p95 and after flip run the microbench.
[22:20] Daniel: we'll include a short runbook for the flip and the verification steps.
[22:30] 
[28:00] Sophie: for the replay sample, do you need the exact user IDs or can we anonymize?
[28:07] Priya: anonymize is fine as long as the request-level GUIDs are stable so we can tie the requests to the audit logs. don't change tokenization or prompt content.
[28:20] Maria: we'll provide GUIDs and the prompt snapshots.
[28:26] 
[32:00] Ethan: question on cost — disabling reuse will increase token costs for us. if we flip the TTL, what ballpark increase should we expect?
[32:10] Priya: depends on hit rate, ballpark 8–15% more token compute on peak windows. we can run the microbench against your trace to give a concrete number.
[32:24] Sophie: ok include cost delta in the bench report.
[32:30] 
[38:00] Ben: recap: Redwood to share trimmed KV dump (no payload) and the replay harness by 2026-03-02; BlueHarbor to run replay on staging (1.8.3 and 1.8.2) and share results by 2026-03-04; short-term config flip (prefixing + TTL 1h) as an emergency mitigation ready to roll and microbench to quantify latency & cost.
[38:25] Raj: agree. we'll do the replay and send request ids.
[38:31] Daniel: also sending SOC2 snapshot and security checklist by 2026-03-03.
[38:36] Sophie: thanks. last ask — can Redwood provide a short summary we can put in our internal incident review for execs? 1 page.
[38:44] Daniel: yes we'll draft a 1-page exec summary and share within 48 hours.
[38:52] 
[45:00] Maria: one more nit — are there any known mythical interactions with third-party model adapters? we use a proprietary reranker that sits between our frontend and Redwood, could that affect the sequence?
[45:12] Priya: adapters are typically stateless wrappers; unless they do prompt concatenation or alter request batching semantics it shouldn't change KV index behavior, but include the adapter logs in the replay package just in case.
[45:30] Ethan: noted.
[46:00] Daniel: thanks everyone — action items noted, we'll follow up with the links and the runbook. Ben will schedule the follow-up post-replay sync.
[46:15] Sophie: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[46:25] Raj: thanks.
[46:30] End of call.
